title: Higher real interest rates in Arland: loanable funds, capital flows, the currency and net exports

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Arland and Belvia are invented countries that trade with each other, and savers in each can buy assets in the other. Arland's currency is the arl and Belvia's is the bel. Both economies begin in long-run equilibrium. Arland's government increases its spending and pays for it by borrowing, which raises its budget deficit. Draw a correctly labeled graph of the loanable funds market in Arland and show the effect of the increase in government borrowing on the real interest rate in Arland.

slips.SLF: Government borrowing raises the real interest rate either way: the demand for loanable funds shifts right (the government borrows more) or the supply shifts left (public saving falls); both are accepted. Shifting supply right would lower it.

rubric.point: A correctly labeled loanable funds graph: Real interest rate on the vertical axis, Quantity of loanable funds on the horizontal axis, a downward-sloping demand and an upward-sloping supply of loanable funds
accept: "Q" or "QLF" for the quantity of loanable funds
DLF and SLF, or D and S, with the market named

rubric.point: The demand for loanable funds shifted to the right, or the supply of loanable funds shifted to the left (government borrowing as lower public saving)
accept: an arrow showing the shift, with the curve named

rubric.point: A higher real interest rate at the new equilibrium (r2 above r1), consistent with the shift drawn
accept: the new equilibrium labeled, with the rate marked on the vertical axis

parts.sample: The graph has Real interest rate (r) on the vertical axis and Quantity of loanable funds on the horizontal axis, with a downward-sloping demand curve DLF1 and an upward-sloping supply curve SLF crossing at r1 and Q1. Government borrowing increases the demand for loanable funds, so DLF1 shifts right to DLF2. At the new equilibrium the real interest rate rises from r1 to r2 and the quantity of loanable funds rises from Q1 to Q2.

parts.label: B(i)
parts.prompt: Based on your answer to part (A), and assuming Belvia's real interest rate does not change, will financial capital flow into Arland or out of Arland?

rubric.point: States that financial capital flows into Arland (consistent with a higher real interest rate in part (A))

parts.sample: Financial capital will flow into Arland.

parts.label: B(ii)

rubric.point: Explains that Arland's real interest rate is now higher than Belvia's, so assets in Arland pay a higher real return and savers (in Belvia and Arland) buy more Arland assets
accept: "Arland bonds now earn more than Belvian bonds after inflation, so Belvians buy Arland bonds"

parts.sample: Arland's real interest rate rose while Belvia's did not, so Arland's real interest rate is now higher relative to Belvia's. Arland bonds and other assets pay a higher real return, so savers in Belvia buy more Arland assets and savers in Arland buy fewer Belvian ones.

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Draw a correctly labeled graph of the foreign exchange market for the arl and show the effect of the change you identified in part (B)(i) on the international value of the arl.

slips.S: Capital flowing into Arland raises the price of the arl: Belvian savers demand more arls, or Arland savers supply fewer arls to buy Belvian assets; both are accepted. Shifting supply right would lower it.

rubric.point: A correctly labeled foreign exchange market for the arl: Price of the arl in bels per arl (or Value of the arl, bels per arl) on the vertical axis, Quantity of arls on the horizontal axis, a downward-sloping demand and an upward-sloping supply of arls
The demand for arls shifted to the right, or the supply of arls shifted to the left, consistent with part (B)(i)
accept: an arrow showing the shift, with the curve named

rubric.point: A higher price of the arl at the new equilibrium (XR2 above XR1): the arl appreciates
accept: the appreciation stated in words with the higher exchange rate shown

parts.sample: The graph has Price of the arl (bels per arl) on the vertical axis and Quantity of arls on the horizontal axis, with demand D1 sloping down and supply S1 sloping up, crossing at XR1. Belvian savers buying Arland assets need arls, so the demand for arls shifts right from D1 to D2. The new equilibrium is at a higher price, XR2: the arl appreciates.

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: Given the change in the value of the arl in part (C), will Arland's net exports increase, decrease or stay the same? Explain.

rubric.point: States that net exports decrease and explains that the appreciated arl makes Arland's exports more expensive for Belvian buyers and Belvian goods cheaper for Arland buyers (exports fall, imports rise)
accept: consistent with the direction shown in part (C)
"Arland goods cost more bels, so Belvians buy fewer; Belvian goods cost fewer arls, so Arland buys more"

parts.sample: Arland's net exports will decrease. Because the arl appreciated, each arl costs more bels, so Arland's goods are more expensive for Belvian buyers and Arland's exports fall, while Belvian goods cost fewer arls, so Arland's imports rise.

parts.label: E
parts.prompt: What happens to the balance of Arland's capital and financial account as a result of the financial capital flow in part (B)(i)?

rubric.point: States that the capital and financial account balance increases (moves toward a surplus), consistent with part (B)(i)
accept: "a larger capital and financial account surplus"

parts.sample: The balance of Arland's capital and financial account increases: foreign purchases of Arland assets are credits, so the capital inflow moves the account toward a larger surplus.
